messages:
maria: Heads-up — staging docs build failing after the content migration. Linkcheck shows a bunch of 404s for anchors in translated pages and some images missing.
jon: saw the same locally. Seems like anchor slugging changed when we moved to the new mdx pipeline.
sam: any example links? I only saw generic 404s in the logs.
maria: here's one from linkcheck: https://docs.redwood.ai/zh/guide/#安装 -> the generated anchor is `#安装` in the HTML which obviously doesn't match the slugified in-page id `#an-zhuang` (pinyin).
kevin: ah yeah, the i18n slugifier step was skipped for markdown headings that have unicode. docusaurus vs mkdocs handle that differently.
lina: also noticed images with paths like `../assets/截图.png` turned into `/docs/assets/%E6%88%AA%E5%9B%BE.png` but our CDN expects `assets/screenshot.png` (we had a normalization script earlier that we didn't port).
maria: ok, plan: 1) quick patch to slugify unicode headings to ascii-compatible ids, 2) normalize image filenames to ascii fallback, 3) re-run linkcheck on staging.
jon: I can open a quick PR with a small transformer during build that applies ascii slugify. thinking of using this node snippet in docusaurus config:
```
const slugify = require('slugify');
function asciiSlug(value) {
  return slugify(value, { lower: true, remove: /[^\w\s-]/g });
}
module.exports = { markdown: { slugify: asciiSlug } };
```
sam: for images I suggest a fallback renamer: when an asset filename contains non-ascii, generate a deterministic ascii name and add a redirect file or map in the manifest.
kevin: I hacked a quick bash loop that emits a mapping and renames files in-place for the build preview:
```
for f in $(find docs -type f -name "*[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]*.png"); do
  nf=$(echo "$f" | iconv -t ascii//TRANSLIT -c | tr ' ' '_' | tr -cd '[:alnum:]._-' )
  mv "$f" "$nf"
  echo "$f -> $nf"
done
```
lina: careful with iconv transliteration — it varies per system. Prefer node-based slugging so CI is deterministic.
maria: agree. jon — can you put the slugify + asset mapping into a small plugin and target a hotfix PR? call out in the PR description what it fixes and add a test case (chinese heading, accented filename).
jon: yep. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/421 (draft). includes unit tests for slugify and a manifest generator for assets.
docs-ci: linkcheck job queued for branch fix/slugify-hotfix. Logs will be posted here when done.
sam: once linkcheck passes, we should run a small smoke test on the zh and fr site builds to verify anchors and images.
kevin: tested locally with the PR branch — anchor ids now `#an-zhuang` -> we replaced with `#an-zhuang`? wait that's wrong, we need consistent ascii versions. jon's slugify produces `an-zhuang` for 安装, which matches the hrefs after transformation.
maria: TL;DR: I merged the draft into hotfix branch and tweaked the asset mapping to write a manifest `assets-manifest.json` for redirects. PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/421
lina: nice. docs-ci: linkcheck passed on staging — 0 anchor failures, 0 missing assets. :tada:
docs-ci: deploy preview available at https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/ (job 2567)
jon: thanks all. I'll follow-up with a short migration note in the docs repo about file naming conventions for localized assets.
maria: can someone add a short blurb to the contributor guide describing the ascii-fallback policy and the recommended filenames? I can draft.
sam: I'll grab it.
kevin: also added a tiny troubleshooting note for maintainers: if you see anchor mismatches, run `node tools/slug-check.js` (included in the PR) which prints problematic headings.
maria: perfect. closing this thread — please ping if anything regresses.
_meta: generated: slack thread about doc anchor/image normalization after migration
